text:
Thinking out loud about the paste path before I write any of it down properly.

The thing I keep coming back to is that the clipboard is shared state and we do not own it. Everything else in the pipeline is ours — the capture renderer, the worker, the prompt, the database — but the clipboard belongs to the whole machine, and the moment we write to it we are stepping on whatever the user had there. So: save the previous contents, write ours, send the paste chord, wait for the target to actually consume it, then put the old contents back. The waiting is the part I keep underestimating. Different apps consume a paste at different speeds and the per-app quirks file exists precisely because there is no single number that works everywhere.

Second thing. If the paste cannot land at all — an elevated window, an admin terminal — the right answer is not an error dialog that throws the text away. Leave it on the clipboard, say so in one line, and let me press Ctrl+V myself. Degrade usefully. An error that loses forty seconds of speech is worse than no feature.

Drei Punkte, die ich noch klären muss: ob der Watchdog wirklich bei hundertzwanzig Sekunden greift, ob ein verpasster Keyup die Aufnahme laufen lässt, und ob die Sprache nach dem Cleanup noch dieselbe ist. Das Letzte ist das Wichtigste — ein deutscher Satz, der auf Englisch zurückkommt, ist der schlimmste mögliche Fehler.

Το τρίτο: να δοκιμάσω τα ελληνικά με το μικρόφωνο των Buds, όχι μόνο με το καλό μικρόφωνο. Αν το narrowband profile χαλάει την ακρίβεια, θέλω να το ξέρω τώρα και όχι στην τρίτη εβδομάδα.

One more note to self: write the row to SQLite before injecting, not after. If the paste fails the transcript still exists, and that is the entire promise of the app — nothing you said is ever lost.
